sources.entry: LanGuard - Wi-Fi off when wired LAN active, back on when unplugged. Edge-based, wake-aware, no admin required.

summary.one_liner: LanGuard is a small native macOS menu-bar app that turns Wi-Fi off when a wired Ethernet link comes up and back on when the cable is unplugged.
summary.what_it_does: It watches wired link state through SystemConfiguration and toggles Wi-Fi power via CoreWLAN, acting only on plug/unplug transitions so a manual Wi-Fi change is respected until the next unplug. It handles wake-from-sleep transitions, lets you choose which wired and Wi-Fi adapters are triggers or controlled, and ignores virtual adapters (VPN, bridge, VMware vmnet) by default. A "Switch to Wi-Fi" action (default shortcut ⌃⌥⌘L) moves traffic to Wi-Fi with a progress window before you unplug, and a master switch pauses automatic toggling. The optional Connection Protection feature installs a root helper and LaunchDaemon guardian to keep a stable address across LAN and Wi-Fi, and includes a panic restore path.
use_cases: automatically turn off Wi-Fi when docked on Ethernet
stop Wi-Fi and wired LAN from competing for default route
switch to Wi-Fi safely before unplugging a cable
keep Mac network connections stable when swapping LAN and Wi-Fi
menu-bar network toggle without admin password
how_to_run: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/LanGuard.app" (optional, if macOS blocks the ad-hoc signed app)
git clone the repository, then cd LanGuard
stack: root helper shell script and LaunchDaemon (optional connection protection)
notable: Edge-based toggling: only reacts to plug/unplug transitions, so manual Wi-Fi changes stick
No admin rights needed for the core Wi-Fi toggle; only optional Connection Protection asks for one admin prompt
Per-interface selection of wired triggers and controlled Wi-Fi adapters
Switch to Wi-Fi action waits for internet reachability before saying it is safe to unplug
Panic restore path via menu, terminal script, or manual commands
caveats: Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later; universal binary for Apple Silicon and Intel
Ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so macOS blocks first launch until you approve it in System Settings
Connection Protection is IPv4 only, needs DHCP on both LAN and Wi-Fi, and conflicts with full-tunnel VPNs
Notarization is listed as roadmap and needs a paid Apple Developer ID
keywords: wifi off when ethernet plugged in
